title: Students on Two Wheels
text:
Last month, a famous science magazine published an article about young people and cycling. The writer visited a school in Krakow, where many students ride bikes to class every day. The article said that cycling makes students feel more awake and happy. It also said that the school has built a new bike parking area with room for two hundred bikes.

The magazine also talked to Anna, a student of sixteen. She said she likes her bike because it is faster than the bus in the morning. However, she sometimes gets wet when it rains. Her teacher thinks that more students will ride bikes in the future, because the city is building new bike paths.

questions.text: How many bikes can the new parking area hold?
What can we infer about Anna's morning journey?
options: She is often late for school.
Cycling is quicker than the bus for her.
She does not like her school.
She walks to school every day.

questions.text: What can we guess about cycling in the city's future?
options: It will close all of its bike paths.
More people will probably cycle there.
The school will stop buying bikes.

vocabulary.definition: not sleepy; alert and full of energy
covered with or full of water or liquid
the time that has not happened yet

paragraph_translations: W zeszłym miesiącu znany magazyn naukowy opublikował artykuł o młodych ludziach i jeździe na rowerze. Autor odwiedził szkołę w Krakowie, gdzie wielu uczniów codziennie jeździ na rowerze do szkoły. Artykuł mówił, że jazda na rowerze sprawia, że uczniowie czują się bardziej rozbudzeni i szczęśliwi. Pisał też, że szkoła zbudowała nowy parking dla rowerów z miejscem na dwieście rowerów.

Magazyn rozmawiał także z Anną, uczennicą szesnastoletnią. Powiedziała, że lubi swój rower, bo rano jest szybszy niż autobus. Czasami jednak moknie, gdy pada deszcz. Jej nauczyciel uważa, że w przyszłości więcej uczniów będzie jeździć na rowerach, ponieważ miasto buduje nowe ścieżki rowerowe.
